  PROBLEM: When `IMPL_CREATED_AFTER_INPUT` is set but malformed, the regex guard silently drops the `created=>` filter: there is no `::warning::` and no `else` branch. The loop then scans up to 10 pages of repo-wide runs filtered only by title. The alt-model copy (around line 5520) has the same pattern.
  WHY: A malformed upstream `created_after` (runner image change, locale `date` surprise) loses the time window silently. The new form can read up to 1000 runs and may miss the late Implement run, leaving the operator no sign.

  PROBLEM: The strict regex match has no `else` arm. A set-but-malformed `IMPL_CREATED_AFTER_INPUT` / `ALT_CREATED_AFTER` leaves `LATE_IMPL_CREATED_FILTER`/`ALT_IMPL_CREATED_FILTER` empty with no diagnostic. `test_smoke_cleanup_closes_late_pr_when_pr_number_empty` only asserts the regex string, which locks in the silent behavior.
  WHY: A failed `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` produces an empty `created_after` (assignments do not trigger `set -e`), so the filter is dropped with no `::warning::`. The 10-page/5-page cap warns only after the API budget is spent.
